content:
The problem I want to solve: I have a lean file. I want to replace all (or most) proofs by sorry. Then such a file would only have comments, definitions, and theorem/example statements, but not their proofs. Similar to how 'header files' in C/C++ only specify declarations, not definitions. Does anyone here have ideas on how to do this?

Why?:

  1. I sometimes want AI to see what theorem statements and definitions are there in a file (so that it can reuse them in other files), but long proofs would flood its context with potentially irrelevant information.
  2. Sometimes I want to see all the theorem statements together without having to scroll back-and-forth, and removing proofs seems like a good way to achieve this.

My solution so far: I have a python script that does this heuristically by matching regexes and checking indentation. But this is a fragile solution. I was wondering if there are existing standard ways to do this.

Could documentation tools and things like LeanArchitect https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22554 not be the right place to make such concise views, if the goal is human readability? For AI tools, maybe dedicated agents like https://github.com/epfl-lara/leanflow could help, as it can separate theorem statements and prove them individually?
